bhsa.note: Verses whose masoretic consonants equal BHSA's exactly and in order; the mean in-order recall over all verses; how many verses carry letters BHSA does not have in that verse; and how many are divided into the same graphical units. Raised through 2026-09-07: 1,143 -> 1,195 when the text column's left overflow stopped being read as margin, -> 1,197 when a '>' in a margin reference stopped being read as a bracket, -> 1,231 when a printed line set as two text objects stopped being read in the order pypdf hands it back. THE EXTRA-TEXT CEILING WAS LOOSENED 61 -> 68 by the first of those was TIGHTENED to 35 by the third, which put the misplaced halves back where they belong, and loosened again to 39 when OVERFLOW_X came down from 80 to 45 - which recovered 9 verses of missing text for those 4. Raised again to 1,283 / 1,220 / 0.979 when the 56 orphan glyphs at x = 0 were given a position instead of being dropped: they are the last letters of words, and 57 verses had been a letter or two short because of them. And to 1,297 / 1,234 when a raised P or D on a clause label stopped hiding the verse number: the last eight missing verses came back and THE BOOK IS NOW COMPLETE, 1,364 of 1,364. And to 1,299 / 1,236 when a masoretic plus stopped being able to nest inside itself. And to 1,314 / 1,250 / 0.984 on 2026-09-09, when the masoretic word Stipp ABBREVIATES stopped being left at its head: where the two forms differ only in their first letter he prints the head, the bar, and the alexandrian word in full, and the shared letters stand once, on the alexandrian side. Sixteen verses were short for that reason alone and fourteen of them are now exact; the extra-text ceiling did not move, so nothing was written that BHSA does not have. 7,9 is the one abbreviation left, its bar being inside a scoped notation and not a bare one, and 2,25 is completed but still short a margin lemma. And to 1,333 / 1,268 / 0.989 the same day, on two more readings of the notation. (27) A bar inside a word can sit in a § ... # notation rather than stand bare, which is what Stipp has to do when the letters the two forms share run over more than one word: 7,9 is the only place, and the masoretic column had HA where BHS reads HA-GANOB RATSOAH WE-NA'OF. (28) An apparatus set inline in the text column pushes what follows it out past the left edge, where the leading-margin loop swallowed it; a ')' in the text with no '(' before it says the line reaches back at least as far as that '(' and the word beyond it. 18 verses, of which 2,25a is the one that showed it. The extra-text ceiling did not move for either. And to 1,339 / 1,274 with (29), the page of the Synopse that is not a page of the text: p. 141 is headed "Jer 43,3-9 mit 4Q72a (4QJer d)" and sets a passage the book has already given, this time beside the Qumran scroll. Read as text it gave every clause of those seven verses twice - 107 extra letters at 43,6 - so THE EXTRA-TEXT CEILING COMES DOWN 30 -> 23, the first time it has been tightened by anything but a fix to the geometry. And to 1,344 / 1,279 with (30), THE NOTATION THAT CLOSES ON THE NEXT COLON. A § ... # states the reach of the bar inside it and the reach is Stipp's, not his colometry's: at 6,6 the § rides on the label of colon d, the bar stands in colon e and the # at its left edge, so read colon by colon the bar was bare, reached one word on each side, and the surplus of the ALEXANDRIAN reading stayed common - HOJ 'IR HA-SHEQER printed in the masoretic column where BHS has only HI' HA-'IR HAPQAD. THE EXTRA-TEXT CEILING COMES DOWN 23 -> 19; 6,6, 20,11, 22,4, 33,2 and 44,12 are the five, and nothing else moved. The carry is bounded by a lookahead rather than by a threshold: a notation reaches only where the next colon puts a bar in it, which keeps it out of Stipp's OTHER notation, the marked stretch with no bar where the two editions have the same consonants and the difference is described in the note. Unbounded it empties the alexandrian cell, which no figure here can see - 21,8c, the book's one reversed pair, ran nine colons to 21,10c. And to 1,365 / 1,299 / 0.996 on 2026-09-10, on two readings that had nothing to do with the notation. (31) A PLUS THAT OPENS IN THE MARGIN. Stipp brackets a plus that wraps to the left end of a printed line; the closing bracket lands in the text column and the opening bracket and the bracketed word land beyond MARGIN_X, so the word was dropped and only its closer survived - LE'MOR at 26,11, BEN-SHAFAN at 43,6. The test is structural and uses no geometry, which is why it reaches where OVERFLOW_X cannot: twelve of these words sit at x = 30.2, where the margin's own lemmas also live. 19 printed lines of the book, 17 verses. (32) A RAISED GLYPH BETWEEN THE HALVES OF A SPLIT LINE. The halves are put back by comparing a line with the one after it, and a line carrying nothing but a Klammerkonstruktion index or a raised Q, P or D falls between them, so the pair was never compared: at 32,35d the index '1' at x = 112.9 kept 32,36's opening formula on the end of 32,35, 28 letters on the wrong verse at each end and the largest deviation in the book. Only a RAISED line may be stepped over; stepping over any line without Hebrew costs eleven verses and loses one from the book. THE EXTRA-TEXT CEILING COMES DOWN 19 -> 16.
